title: HydroGraphNet: Interpretable Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for Flood Forecasting
why_relevant: Flood-specific primary source for autoregressive graph forecasting with auxiliary physical constraints. Its rollout training and physics-lite regularization ideas transfer well to this competition.
extracted_technique: Encode-process-decode graph surrogate with pushforward training, auxiliary hydraulic states, and mild conservation regularization.
query: site:docs.nvidia.com PhysicsNeMo HydroGraphNet flood forecasting pushforward training
takeaway: The transferable lesson is not to predict water level in isolation. Jointly modeling auxiliary states and using rollout-aware training is likely to improve stability over long horizons.

title: Predicting the urban stormwater drainage system state using the Graph-WaveNet
why_relevant: This is the closest architecture match to the competition: rainfall-driven urban drainage forecasting on graph-structured infrastructure with long causal horizons.
extracted_technique: Dilated causal temporal convolutions plus graph supports and adaptive adjacency for urban drainage state forecasting.
query: predicting the urban stormwater drainage system state using the Graph-WaveNet
takeaway: This is the strongest backbone candidate for the competition. The main adaptation is turning the single-domain drainage graph into a heterograph with 1D nodes, 2D nodes, and coupling edges.

title: FloodGNN-GRU: a spatio-temporal graph neural network for flood prediction
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed flood forecasting evidence that recurrent graph state models can be strong when rainfall forcing and spatial interactions both matter.
extracted_technique: Graph recurrent forecasting with rainfall forcing, static terrain features, and causal next-step prediction over flood states.
query: site:cambridge.org FloodGNN-GRU flood prediction rainfall graph neural network
takeaway: A recurrent graph model is a credible challenger, especially if directional transport matters more than very long convolutional receptive fields. Validation must be full rollout, otherwise it will look better than it really is.
